figures.title: The policy and effect-consumer boundary
figures.description: Grade settings are authoritative. The host supplies observations to a pure reducer, its effects authorize adapter operations, and operation receipts return as events.

figures.title: Latest-demand preparation scheduling
figures.description: The latest requested signature shares one physical preparation slot. Preview leaves the running job occupied; its final receipt starts the newest successor.

figures.title: Node output and installation policy
figures.description: Output is derived as current, preview, pending, or error. Only a full-quality installation for current demand can render; new demand can leave error.

figures.title: Helper process lifecycle
figures.description: All helper phases are explicit from startup through physical exit and cleanup. Protocol v2 uses a session UUID in both directions and a token in hello; job IDs and deadline stages correlate receipts. Failed can still close on shutdown; closed is absorbing.

figures.title: Production two-bank publication
figures.description: The inactive bank's five Stage 2/3 roles are staged before selector readback and delivery. Repair enters the same staging phase after confirmed closure. Selection or delivery failure requests selector restoration before closure. Each closure phase permits one retry, and all outcomes share one terminal state.

figures.title: Resource adoption and retirement
figures.description: Adoption is a predicate. Disposal fences and detaches subscriptions before observation; undo-retained resources take a fake-user branch, while removal requires eviction and a fresh eligibility check. Terminal is shared by retention, removal, and ineligible outcomes.

figures.title: Observer handoff policy
figures.description: Observer installation promotes only a matching pending token. Separate states show pending installation with and without a current observer; reset preserves the monotonic serial.

figures.title: Gesture participation in the runtime coordinator
figures.description: The runtime tracks armed, active, finishing-armed, and finishing-active states. Scalar policy decisions release only the final active participant in a node.

figures.title: Render preflight authorization
figures.description: Only the active ticket inside its exclusive scope may publish. Release requires the requested scene and time, exact Grade signature, and current outputs. Mismatches fail with an error; released and failed are terminal.

figures.title: Bake request and publication policy
figures.description: A correlated request progresses from queueing through native evaluation, admitted publication, and activation. Stale results are discarded; running cancellation retains ownership until a final receipt. Failed or stale publication and activation authorize rollback. Terminal is absorbing.

figures.title: Preparation and node output workflow
figures.description: A rapid settings edit retains the last installation as a preview while one worker prepares the latest demand. Existing publication effects append a native template, bind the current payload, validate and install it. A current preparation, template, binding, or installation failure selects visible error output.

figures.title: Helper process workflow
figures.description: The runtime checks the protocol v2 hello token and session. A matching probe result is published and enters ready with an idle work slot. Ordinary work is submitted afterward. The policy correlates work receipts by job ID and phase, and shutdown escalation follows the current deadline stage.

figures.title: Bank publication workflow
figures.description: All five parameter roles are staged before one selector publishes the complete bank. Reuse requires clean packed pixels that match the prepared content receipts. Staging appends a template when the Grade graph needs replacement. Each closure phase allows one retry.

figures.title: Resource retirement workflow
figures.description: Disposal fences and detaches before observation. An undo-retained resource receives fake-user protection; otherwise an eligible resource is evicted, rechecked, and removed, while protected or in-use resources are retained.

figures.title: Observer and gesture workflow
figures.description: The coordinator installs and hands off an observer, tracks pointer movement, defers finish until native observation, and releases only the last active node participant.

figures.title: Render preflight workflow
figures.description: The main thread reconciles the requested time, then validates the live scene and time, Grade signature, and output. Publication rechecks the ticket's native render lease and exclusive access. The failure path attempts to install visible error output before delivering the failed ticket.

figures.title: Native bake and managed Image publication workflow
figures.description: Each request uses a unique artifact directory with a fixed bake.exr output. The execution runtime matches receipts by session and job ID. The manager verifies the result signature and retains a ready artifact while publication is deferred. Dependency generations guard freshness. Publication, activation, and rollback share one admitted commit scope. Shared readers are synchronized after activation or restoration.

figures.title: Color authoring and evaluated constraints
figures.description: A synchronous runtime composes cyclic hue edits and sparse ownership claims through per-handle policy effects, then the adapter commits settings and claims in one scope. Peak and actual node-owned time changes clear claims. Invalid animated samples use closest-angle and radial constraints without rewriting keyframes.
